units.text: A ⟦0⟧filesystem⟦1⟧ is a section of a disk, either on the local host or mounted from a remote host over a network. Searching network filesystems can be slow, so it is common to make ⟦2⟧ avoid them.
units.sourceHTML: A filesystem is a section of a disk, either on the local host or mounted from a remote host over a network. Searching network filesystems can be slow, so it is common to make find avoid them.

units.text: There are two ways to avoid searching certain filesystems. One way is to tell ⟦0⟧ to only search within the same filesystem as the start-point currently being searched:
units.sourceHTML: There are two ways to avoid searching certain filesystems. One way is to tell find to only search within the same filesystem as the start-point currently being searched:

units.text: Ignore files on other devices. Do not visit or search inside mount points. Do not search inside directories within other file systems even if they are the target of a symbolic link and ⟦0⟧ is following symbolic links (e.g. due to the ‘⟦1⟧’ or ‘⟦2⟧’ option).
units.sourceHTML: Ignore files on other devices. Do not visit or search inside mount points. Do not search inside directories within other file systems even if they are the target of a symbolic link and find is following symbolic links (e.g. due to the ‘-L’ or ‘-H’ option).

units.text: Visit mount points but not their children (that is, don’t descend into directories on other devices). Using ⟦0⟧ has the same effect as ‘⟦1⟧’.
units.sourceHTML: Visit mount points but not their children (that is, don’t descend into directories on other devices). Using -mount -xdev has the same effect as ‘-mount’.

units.text: You can use ‘⟦0⟧’ with the ‘⟦1⟧’ directive to see the types of your filesystems. ‘⟦2⟧’ is usually used with ‘⟦3⟧’ to avoid searching remote filesystems (see ⟦4⟧Directories⟦5⟧).
units.sourceHTML: You can use ‘-printf’ with the ‘%F’ directive to see the types of your filesystems. ‘-fstype’ is usually used with ‘-prune’ to avoid searching remote filesystems (see Directories).
